title: Tighten RBAC for provisioning actions (least privilege) + security review checklist
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
project: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
We are expanding provisioning automation (Fleet Provisioner + CLI triggers + pause/resume + stage re-runs). Current RBAC/IAM permissions are too broad across:
- Control plane API endpoints that start/modify provisioning runs
- Operator CLI authz
- Provisioner service role used to orchestrate Terraform, bootstrap, and validation

This ticket tightens RBAC to least-privilege, defines role boundaries, and adds a lightweight security review checklist so new stages/permissions don’t quietly expand scope.

Primary goals:
1) Ensure only the right principals can trigger/modify provisioning runs, and only for allowed pool(s)/env(s).
2) Reduce blast radius: provisioner should not have general cloud-admin privileges.
3) Have an auditable path for admin-only / break-glass actions (pause/resume overrides, validation bypasses, etc.).

Out of scope:
- Re-architecting the provisioning orchestration model (covered by ADR-0142)
- Full customer-facing RBAC (this is internal/operator-facing)

Stakeholders:
- Security: Marcus Lin (approver), Kevin Osei (audit/logging requirements)
- Platform/Control Plane: Ethan Park
- Infra Fleet: Vanessa Ortiz, Nina Petrova
- SRE: Rafael Mendes

Acceptance criteria:
- [x] Control plane provisioning endpoints enforce RBAC by action + scope (pool_id / env / region where applicable)
- [x] Provisioner service cloud IAM reduced to minimum required (Terraform apply, image pull, cluster bootstrap, metrics/logging)
- [x] Separate roles for: (a) view status, (b) trigger run, (c) pause/resume / stage re-run, (d) break-glass actions
- [x] All privileged actions emit audit log entries with actor, action, scope, correlation_id
- [x] Security review checklist added to repo (and referenced from runbook/PR template section)

Implementation notes / decisions:
- RBAC model: "provisioning:*" actions are split by verbs:
  - provisioning.run.view
  - provisioning.run.create
  - provisioning.run.modify (pause/resume, rerun stage)
  - provisioning.run.breakglass (admin-only; requires reason)
- Scope enforcement:
  - Non-admin operators limited to specific env (staging vs prod) via role bindings
  - Pool scoping via allowlist mapping in control plane (initially by pool_id; future: customer_id/team ownership)
- IAM for provisioner service:
  - Removed wildcard permissions on compute/network where not required
  - Restricted secret access to specific secret paths; no list-all permissions
  - Restricted artifact registry access to read-only + specific repos for golden image / helm charts
- Audit logging requirements (per Kevin Osei):
  - Include correlation_id (provisioning run ID)
  - Include request_id, actor principal, source (CLI vs API), and reason for break-glass
  - Logs retained per standard control plane audit policy

Security review checklist (minimum):
- Verify new permissions are scoped (resource-level) and do not use * where avoidable
- Verify privileged endpoints require admin role + explicit reason string
- Verify break-glass actions alert (non-paging) to #eng-sre + create INT ticket
- Verify audit logs are emitted for create/modify/break-glass actions
- Verify secrets access is least privilege (read only; no list; env-scoped)
- Verify terraform runner role cannot assume arbitrary roles
- Verify staging/prod separation: no cross-env write permissions
- Verify runbook documents manual override + escalation path

Links:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/48243 (IAM restriction + credential rotation + checklist)
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/48233 (authz checks for trigger/status endpoints)
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/48246 (pause/resume admin-only + audit logs)

Rollout:
- Land changes behind provisioning feature flag where applicable
- Validate in staging with oncall/SRE (attempt: view-only token cannot trigger; operator token can trigger; non-admin cannot break-glass)
- Promote to prod after 24h of staging success and no blocked operator workflows

Risks / mitigations:
- Risk: over-tightening blocks pilot execution.
  - Mitigation: document temporary allowlist process + audit + expiration; keep manual override path available with admin approval.
- Risk: drift between control plane RBAC and cloud IAM expectations.
  - Mitigation: add integration test that exercises common operator flows using least-privilege roles; run in CI nightly for staging.
